sources.Sigma_ref: v14 galactic specialization, Σ_ref = 1 M_⊙ pc^{-2}

estimator_assumptions.sigma_from_a: σ = sqrt(a_tot R_e / 4) with a_tot = a_bar + a_ind
estimator_assumptions.Sigma_bar: mean within R_e: M_*/(2 π R_e^2); not a published profile
estimator_assumptions.anisotropy: Wolf estimator; weak anisotropy sensitivity near r_1/2
estimator_assumptions.no_refit: A, n_g, alpha_eff, xi_c window fixed; no optimization

systems_literature.name: NGC1052-DF2

distance.notes: SBF D=19.0±1.7 Mpc; paper adopts ≈20 Mpc with NGC 1052. TRGB re-measurements exist (Danieli et al. 2020 ≈22 Mpc); we adopt the homogeneous 20 Mpc group scale and propagate ±1.7 Mpc. Shen et al. 2023 quote 21.7 Mpc in some comparisons.

M_star.citation: van Dokkum et al. 2018, Nature; M/L_V≈2.0
M_star.notes: M_stars ≈ 2×10^8 M_⊙ at D=20 Mpc; ~25% M/L systematic folded into unc.

R_e.citation: van Dokkum et al. 2018, Nature (R_e=22.6'' → 2.2 kpc at 20 Mpc)
R_e.notes: Major-axis half-light radius; Sérsic n=0.6. Scales ∝ D.

sigma_obs.notes: Primary stellar σ. GC-based values: van Dokkum et al. 2018 σ_intr=3.2^{+5.5}_{-3.2} (90% UL 10.5); revised GC analyses exist. Keim et al. 2026 quote a broadening-corrected 6.1^{+3.7}_{-3.1} for cross-check; we retain Danieli 2019 as the published primary stellar measurement.

sigma_baryon_lit.citation: Danieli et al. 2019; van Dokkum et al. 2018 (stars alone ~7–8 km/s)
sigma_baryon_lit.notes: Literature pure-baryon expectation; we recompute via Wolf below.

systems_literature.profile_limitation: No published high-resolution mass surface-density profile used. Mean Σ within R_e computed from M_* and R_e (mass-follows-light).

systems_literature.name: NGC1052-DF4

distance.citation: van Dokkum et al. 2019, ApJL, 874, L5 (SBF 19.9±2.8); Danieli et al. 2020 TRGB ≈20.0
distance.notes: Adopt D=20 Mpc on the same group scale as DF2.

R_e.citation: van Dokkum et al. 2019, ApJL (R_e=1.6 kpc; n=0.79)
R_e.notes: Scales ∝ D. Shen et al. 2023 quote 16.5'' = 1.6 kpc.

sigma_obs.notes: Stellar σ_stars=8.0^{+2.3}_{-1.9} km/s. Combined star+GC fiducial σ_f=6.3^{+2.5}_{-1.6} km/s also reported; we use stellar as primary. GC-only van Dokkum et al. 2019: 4.2^{+4.4}_{-2.2} km/s.

systems_literature.profile_limitation: No published radial Σ profile used; mean Σ within R_e from M_* and R_e.

systems_literature.name: NGC1052-DF9

distance.citation: Keim et al. 2026, ApJ (arXiv:2603.15860); trail scale Keim et al. 2025
distance.notes: Expected distance from position along the NGC 1052 trail. Results are weakly distance-dependent (σ_baryon ∝ D^{1/2} scaling cancels in mass comparison at leading order; see Keim et al. App. B).

M_star.citation: Keim et al. 2026 (from Gannon et al. 2023 photometry; M/L_g=2.2)
M_star.notes: Total stellar mass 1.4×10^8 M_⊙; half-light stellar mass 0.71±0.16×10^8.

R_e.citation: Keim et al. 2026; Gannon et al. 2023 (11.1'' at 20.6 Mpc → 1.1 kpc)
R_e.notes: Circularized effective radius used with Wolf estimator.

sigma_obs.notes: Gravitational σ after subtracting σ_broadening=5.4±2 and σ_binaries=2.3±0.6 from fit σ_fit=8.7^{+3.4}_{-3.7}.

sigma_baryon_lit.citation: Keim et al. 2026 (Wolf from M_e,* alone)
sigma_baryon_lit.notes: Literature pure-baryon expectation from stellar mass within R_e.

systems_literature.profile_limitation: No published Σ profile; mean Σ within R_e from M_* and R_e.

systems_literature.name: FCC224

distance.citation: Buzzo et al. 2025, A&A (arXiv:2502.05405); Tang et al. 2025a photometry at 20 Mpc
distance.notes: Fornax outskirts; systemic velocity 1405±3 km/s consistent with cluster. GCLF and stellar mass quoted at 20 Mpc. Distance unc. ~typical Fornax ladder.

M_star.citation: Buzzo et al. 2025; Tang et al. 2025a: log(M_*/M_⊙)=8.24±0.04

R_e.citation: Buzzo et al. 2025; Tang et al. 2025a: R_e=1.89±0.01 kpc
R_e.notes: UDG within uncertainties; μ_g,0=23.97±0.03; b/a=0.64; n=0.75.

sigma_obs.notes: Published σ_stars=7.82^{+6.74}_{-4.36} km/s after subtracting σ_broadening=6.9±2.6 from raw σ_galaxy=10.43±5.76 km/s (Buzzo et al. 2025 §3.3.1). Asymmetric 1σ adopted as published; not a fabricated symmetric error. Galaxy is DM-deficient within 1 R_e per authors. Slow prolate rotation 7.5±3.0 km/s reported (not subtracted here; see systematics).

sigma_baryon_lit.citation: Buzzo et al. 2025 (stars-alone Jeans/SMHM comparison value)

systems_literature.profile_limitation: No published full Σ profile used; mean Σ within R_e from M_* and R_e. KCWI FoV covers only ~0.4 R_e,circ for population gradients.

future_targets.name: NGC1052 trail members (excl. DF2/DF4/DF9)
future_targets.reason: Keim et al. 2025/2026: remaining trail galaxies up to ~100× fainter; radial velocities partially available but internal kinematics not yet of KCWI/MUSE quality comparable to DF2/DF4/DF9.
future_targets.citation: van Dokkum et al. 2022a; Keim et al. 2025, 2026

future_targets.name: FCC240
future_targets.reason: Buzzo et al. 2026 (arXiv:2605.24099): close companion to FCC 224; analogue discussion; published kinematics of residual-sample quality not adopted here as primary.

future_targets.name: Tidal-dwarf candidates (e.g. NGC 5291N, etc.)
future_targets.reason: Classic TDGs can be DM-poor but generally have rotation-supported HI kinematics and different formation channels; not included without a homogeneous pressure-supported σ of UDG quality.
future_targets.citation: Lelli et al. 2015; Bournaud et al. 2007 (context only)

future_targets.name: Almost-dark HI clouds / HI-bearing UDGs
future_targets.reason: Interesting for low-Σ shoulder of Φ(ξ) but require published stellar or GC dispersions of comparable quality; list as future targets only.

residual_summary.classification_note: For every system in this small sample, the frozen intermediate-regime UMM power-law predicts a line-of-sight dispersion more than 2σ above the observed value (model systematically high). The pure-baryon column is consistent with the data within uncertainties. This is an illustrative first estimate on a small sample; systematics remain significant, but the direction of the residual is uniform.
residual_summary.honesty: Illustrative first estimate; small sample (N=4); systematics remain significant (distance, M/L, residual rotation, possible tides, mean-Σ proxy for local Σ_bar, thin-disk specialization applied to pressure-supported systems).
